title: Bullion knot
subtitle: A coiled knot that forms a raised bar or rounded bud shape
excerpt: Bullion knot wraps the thread many times around the needle to form a coiled cylinder that lies as a raised bar on the fabric. The number of wraps determines the length of the bar. Groups of bullion knots make three-dimensional rose and bud motifs.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), knotted stitches chapter (Project Gutenberg #20776). Weldon's Practical Needlework, Vol. 5 (1889), bullion rose entry.

glossaryTerms.definition: The number of thread wraps on the needle before insertion. More wraps make a longer coiled bar; the coil count must be matched to the distance between the entry and exit holes.

heroPrompt: Bullion knots forming a small dimensional rose in dusty pink stranded cotton on cream linen, the coiled bars arranged in a spiral, side lighting showing the raised texture.

content.text: Bullion knot builds a raised coil by matching the

to the stitch length. The needle goes in and comes back up a stitch-length away, but is not pulled through. Thread is wrapped around the exposed needle the required number of times, then the needle is pulled through the coil and the coil is eased back down onto the fabric.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton 2 strands; perle 12 for finer coils; milliner's needle preferred

items.label: Fabric
items.value: Tightly woven linen or cotton (loose weave splits under the needle)

items.label: Needle
items.value: Milliner's needle size 3 to 5 (same diameter along the shaft for smooth coil release)

content.text: Bring the thread up at A. Insert the needle at B (the desired bar length away) and bring the tip back up at A without pulling through.
Wrap the thread clockwise around the needle, counting the wraps. The coil should cover the A-to-B distance when unspooled.
Hold the coil firmly against the fabric and pull the needle through the coil.
Ease the coil back toward B and insert the needle at B to complete. The coil should lie flat along the AB distance.

items.symptom: The coil bunches at one end and leaves a gap at the other
items.cause: Too many or too few wraps for the stitch length.
items.fix: Count the wraps carefully for the first bullion and adjust. The coil must be exactly the right length to reach from A to B without slack or tension.

items.symptom: The needle sticks when pulling through the coil
items.cause: Using a needle that tapers toward the eye.
items.fix: Use a milliner's needle, which is the same width along the full shaft. The coil releases cleanly from a uniform-width needle.

content.text: Bullion knots are the building blocks of dimensional bullion roses. Groups of bullions arranged in a fan or spiral form rosebuds and open roses in Brazilian embroidery and South African raised embroidery.
